I'm 58 years old, been farming this same 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and add up the costs at the shop, but to be honest I mostly do what has always worked, and I watch what my neighbors do. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so it's just me and my husband in the fields now.

My wheat went in last October right after we threshed the corn. I planted the same improved variety I've used for three years — 7.5 kilograms of seed per mu. At planting I spread one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Now that spring is here, I'll topdress with 25 kilograms of urea per mu when the wheat greens up. Last year I only used 20 kilograms and the plants looked a bit pale by jointing, so I'm adding more this time. I'd rather spend the extra 20 yuan per mu than risk losing yield — with only 4.1 mu, every jin of grain matters. I irrigate the wheat three times: at green-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. The well pump costs electricity, but three times is what everyone around here does. Two sprays — herbicide first, then another if I see aphids or the leaves start spotting.

For the summer corn, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in early June. Everyone switched to hybrid corn years ago — the stalks are thicker and the ears are fatter. I use 2 kilograms of seed per mu. I put down 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then side-dress with 20 kilograms of urea per mu when the corn is at knee height. Two irrigations — one when it's shooting up, one when the ears are filling. Two pesticide sprays. I rotary till before both crops, always have, though some young folks are trying no-tillage. I'm not risking it on my land.

With 4.1 mu, I watch every yuan. But I learned my lesson from my cousin two years ago — she cut back on fertilizer to save money and her wheat barely made 400 kilograms per mu. I figure if I get 550 kilograms per mu of wheat and 600 kilograms per mu of corn, that's enough to feed the family and have some left to sell.
